The dashboard and the alert rule both exist now. I haven't opened the dashboard in Kibana, so I don't know how the panels render. I also haven't checked whether the rule has run yet, or whether its 5xx query matches any documents.

**What the data holds:** the data view has 30 or so fields. These are the ones I used:
- `@timestamp`
- `response`, the HTTP status code
- `bytes`
- `geo.src` and `geo.dest`
- `extension`
- `machine.os`
- `clientip`
- `url`
- `agent`

**Dashboard:** `EFF-882bdcc5 Web logs overview` (id `69916d1c-8cb8-4e55-b36b-230571374b28`) has six panels and defaults to the last 7 days:
- Three metric panels: total requests, 5xx responses, and average bytes per request.
- A line chart of requests over time.
- A bar chart of requests by response code.
- A bar chart of the top 10 source countries.

All six panels use ES|QL queries against `kibana_sample_data_logs`, not the saved data view. I did this because that is the form the Dashboards API documents for inline charts.

**Alert rule:** `EFF-882bdcc5 5xx spike` (id `fd16f3ea-0644-482b-af44-689c0f8cfb05`) is enabled and checks every minute. It fires when more than 10 documents in the last 5 minutes have a `response.keyword` starting with "5". It's an Elasticsearch query rule with no actions attached, so when it fires it only creates an alert and notifies nobody.
